headline: Crude Rises Toward $117 as Hormuz Tanker Attacks Escalate Middle East Risks
summary: Crude oil rose to between $115 and $117 a barrel following escalated attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and reported strikes targeting Saudi oil infrastructure and airports.
why: Crude oil prices directly affect headline global inflation, transportation costs, and central bank monetary policy trajectories.

impacts.name: Brent Crude
impacts.why: Supply disruption fears and maritime transit risk in the Strait of Hormuz push oil prices higher.

impacts.name: Energy
impacts.why: Elevated benchmark crude prices directly enhance upstream oil and gas revenues.

why_moved: Oil prices jumped toward $117 a barrel due to attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and reported military strikes on regional facilities.
